music.title: What We Leave Behind
music.description:
"What We Leave Behind" is about the trade-offs we make in the name of progress.

The song asks a simple but uncomfortable question: In our rush to find tomorrow, what are we sacrificing today? Face-to-face conversations replaced by text replies. Time wasted together traded for efficiency. Connection lost somewhere between the screens.

It's not anti-technology or nostalgic for some imagined past. It's about recognizing that the things we outgrew might have been the best we ever knew — and wondering if we'll realize it too late.

Does moving forward mean leaving behind the things that mattered most?

music.title: Everything and Nothing at All
music.description:
"Everything and Nothing at All" is about drowning in a world designed to keep you busy but leave you empty.

We consume, we scroll, we work, we spend — but we're not really here. The song captures that modern exhaustion of having more access, more information, more everything, while feeling increasingly disconnected from what matters.

It's the paradox of our time: the world gets bigger while our world gets smaller. The noise keeps coming, but the quiet is what's calling.
A question worth asking: If you turned it all off, what would you hear?

music.title: Just Another Day
music.description:
"Just Another Day" is about the moments we rush through without realizing they're the ones we'll want back.
Morning coffee. Shared laughter. A simple smile before heading out to work. These aren't just routines but the architecture of a shared life. The song captures that tension between hurrying through the day and wanting to hold onto it, between the ordinary and the irreplaceable.
It's a reminder that love lives in the small stuff. The kind of moments that don't feel like much until you understand they're everything.

music.title: Life I Could've Had
music.description: A song about big dreams and beautiful reality.

music.title: Familiar Strangers
music.description: “Familiar Strangers” is an alternative track exploring the quiet distance of modern life, how we search for connection through the glow of our screens while drifting further from one another. Inspired by a journal entry about the way strangers online shape our choices, the song blends atmospheric indie textures with lyrics about digital longing, fractured identities, and the ache of wanting something real in a world of static and reflections. Human-ideated and AI-assisted, it captures the tension of living close to everyone and no one at the same time.

music.description: Available soon on Spotify and Apple Music. An upbeat song about the messy push-and-pull of human nature in relationships — wanting closeness but fearing the fall.
music.inspiration: Based on the beautiful messiness of human relationships.

projects.title: Photo Bookshelf
projects.summary: A community-built recommendation site for photography books.
projects.description:
Photo Bookshelf started with a long thread on social media where a new photographer asked which books they should read. Watching the replies pile up made me realize how hard it actually is to find good photography books, and how much of that knowledge lives in scattered conversations instead of one place.

So I built photobookshelf.com: a community-based recommendation site for photography books, plus the books that inspire or help a photographer see. Every book on the shelf was put forward by someone, and contributors get their own shelf page with a personal note about why those books matter to them.

The site pairs a rotating featured pick with browsing and filtering by type, publisher, availability, and level, so you can move from celebrated classics to independent and self-published work in the same place.

projects.title: Parametra Music
projects.summary: Parametra Music is my ongoing experiment in creating songs with AI.
projects.description:
Parametra Music is my ongoing experiment in creating songs with AI and treating music like parametric design. Instead of starting with a traditional instrument-first workflow, I start with raw material: journal notes, late-night thoughts, conversations, observations, and the small contradictions that show up in everyday life. Those become lyric fragments, themes, structure, and a “vibe,” and I use AI (Suno) to translate those parameters into finished tracks.

My value add is the human part: choosing what the song is about, shaping the story, editing lines until they feel honest, and making the creative calls similar to how a producer would make them, what stays, what goes, what the mood is, and what the listener should feel by the end. The goal isn’t perfection, it’s exploration: what happens when a creative technologist approaches songwriting like rule-setting and iteration.

Releases span multiple genres under one identity, starting with On The Edge (New Wave) and It’s Just My Nature (Alt-Country), with more to come.

projects.title: The Poetic AI
projects.summary: An experiment in combining poetry and parametric art.
projects.description: The Poetic AI is my ongoing experiment in pairing language and code—AI-assisted poems matched with parametric, generative artwork that’s shaped by the same themes, mood, and “parameters” inside each piece.

about.name: Thomas Alan Smilie
about.subtitle: A creative technologist in Japan, exploring what me + technology can create.
about.content:
I’ve always made things—with cameras, code, and curiosity. My path has taken me from a sales rep in Tokyo to a university webmaster, a commercial photographer, and now a digital marketing manager. The titles have changed, but the impulse remains the same: to create something honest with whatever tools are available.

Living in Japan taught me that patience and imperfection tell the best stories. I learned to see light through a film camera and structure through early HTML. Today, as a Creative Technologist, I’m exploring where those disciplines meet.

Whether I'm capturing a moment on the streets of Okinawa or turning journal entries into songs with AI, I’m still chasing that line where art and code blur into something human.
